Done. The Set-Cookie merge bug is fixed and covered by a regression test.

## Root cause
`src/context.ts:421-426` (before) ran `_res.headers.delete('set-cookie')` whenever `c.res` already existed, wiping the incoming handler Response's own cookies before appending only the middleware/old cookies. The handler's `Set-Cookie` was always lost.

Also verified `Headers.entries()` yields each `set-cookie` value as a separate entry (Node 24), so merging inside that loop would duplicate old cookies once per entry.

## Fix — `src/context.ts:414-428`
```ts
if (k === 'content-type' || k === 'set-cookie') {
  continue
}
_res.headers.set(k, v)
...
for (const cookie of this.#res.headers.getSetCookie()) {
  _res.headers.append('set-cookie', cookie)
}
```
- Skips `set-cookie` in the header-copy loop (no deletion, no duplicates).
- Appends existing `c.res` cookies exactly once after the loop.
- Other-header precedence (`_res` wins) and content-type behavior unchanged.

## Tests — `src/context.test.ts`
- Updated the test that encoded the old behavior: `src/context.test.ts:430` now asserts merge order `[...newCookies, ...cookies]` (3 cookies).
- Added regression test `src/context.test.ts:447`: middleware cookie on `c.res` + handler `Response` with its own `set-cookie` → both survive (`length === 2`, both contained). Pre-fix this yields only the middleware cookie.

## Verification
```
pnpm exec vp test --run src/context.test.ts
Tests  64 passed (64)
```
Also ran the adjacent cookie/language middleware suites (they exercise this setter): `2 files passed, 67 tests passed`. Changes are unstaged; no commits made.
